concerns.text: The ‘GPU escape hatch’ (re‑run on Kaggle GPU if a model exceeds 60 s) introduces a hardware confound: some models may be evaluated on CPU, others on GPU, violating Principle VII (Architectural Fidelity Isolation) and threatening causal attribution to model architecture.

Technical‑intent entities are identified by a zero‑shot classifier with a fixed confidence threshold (≥0.7). This indirect method may not reliably capture the construct “technical intent”, especially given only a 50‑sample gold‑standard for validation, raising construct‑validity concerns.

The plan requires ≥500 commit‑doc pairs but does not justify that this sample size provides adequate statistical power for the Friedman test to detect medium‑sized effects across three models; a power analysis is missing.
Multiple metrics (intent precision, surface precision, hallucination rate) will be tested, yet no correction for multiple comparisons is described, increasing the risk of Type I errors.

Surface‑entity regexes are limited to file paths, function signatures, and version numbers; many other surface changes (e.g., class names, variable names) will be missed, compromising the validity of the ‘surface’ construct.

Verification of generated surface entities via `git grep` may yield false negatives for entities that exist but are not literal string matches (e.g., aliased imports), leading to inflated hallucination rates.
